struct.name: WID_STAT
struct.doc: Widget status, the second word of the standard widget configuration block (`p_wid_stat`). Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: WID_ERR_UPPER
struct.doc: Widget error address, upper word (`p_wid_err_upper`); the lower word is the census register `bus_err`. Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: WID_INT_UPPER
struct.doc: Widget interrupt destination, upper word (`p_wid_int_upper`); the lower word is the census register `intr_dst_target_id`. Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: WID_TST_PIN_CTRL
struct.doc: Test pin control (`p_wid_tst_pin_ctrl`), the one slot of the bridge-specific block between the response words and the address-lock error register. Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: PCI_ERR_UPPER
struct.doc: PCI bus error address, upper word (`p_pci_err_upper`); the lower word is the census register `pci_bus_addr`. Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: BUF_ADDR_MATCH
struct.doc: Buffer address match registers: sixteen pairs, upper word then lower word, sixteen bytes per pair (`p_buf_addr_match[n].upper` and `.lower`). Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: BUF_FLUSH_W_TOUCH
struct.doc: Performance monitor block n, word 0 (`p_buf_count[n].flush_w_touch`): eight blocks of eight words, 0x40 bytes apart. The header comment marks them even-numbered buffers only. The register names are the only description. Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: BUF_FLUSH_WO_TOUCH
struct.doc: Performance monitor block n, word 1 (`flush_wo_touch`). Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: BUF_INFLIGHT
struct.doc: Performance monitor block n, word 2 (`inflight`). Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: BUF_PREFETCH
struct.doc: Performance monitor block n, word 3 (`prefetch`). Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: BUF_TOTAL_PCI_RETRY
struct.doc: Performance monitor block n, word 4 (`total_pci_retry`). Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: BUF_MAX_PCI_RETRY
struct.doc: Performance monitor block n, word 5 (`max_pci_retry`). Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: BUF_MAX_LATENCY
struct.doc: Performance monitor block n, word 6 (`max_latency`). Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: BUF_CLEAR_ALL
struct.doc: Performance monitor block n, word 7 (`clear_all`). Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: PCIX_TIMEOUT
struct.doc: PCI-X timeout (`p_pcix_timeout`), the eighth word of the PCI-X register block that follows the seven census registers. Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: PCIX_READ_BUF_ADDR
struct.doc: PCI-X read buffer n, address word (`p_pcix_read_buf_64[n].p_buf_addr`); the attribute word of the same buffer follows it. Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: PCIX_READ_BUF_ATTR
struct.doc: PCI-X read buffer n, attribute word (`p_buf_attr`). Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: PCIX_WRITE_BUF_ADDR
struct.doc: PCI-X write buffer n, address word (`p_pcix_write_buf_64[n].p_buf_addr`); the attribute, valid and one unused word follow at eight-byte steps. Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: PCIX_WRITE_BUF_ATTR
struct.doc: PCI-X write buffer n, attribute word (`p_buf_attr`). Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: PCIX_WRITE_BUF_VALID
struct.doc: PCI-X write buffer n, valid word (`p_buf_valid`). Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: INT_ATE_MP
struct.doc: Second copy of the internal translation entries with manual parity generation (`p_int_ate_ram_mp`); the census register `int_ate` is the automatic-parity copy. No IRIX routine reaches this range. Offset, width and name are the header definition. Access direction is not stated by the header or by any code read; nothing in the SN2 driver or the IRIX objects reaches this register, so its behaviour is unknown.

struct.name: ARB_REG
struct.doc: Arbitration: request wait tick and enable, grant freeze, bridge high and low priority enables, and device-broke bits (names only).

struct.name: BUF_FLUSH_WO_TOUCH_REG
struct.doc: Performance counter, per even buffer block: flushes with no data used. A word write clears it.

struct.name: BUF_FLUSH_W_TOUCH_REG
struct.doc: Performance counter, per even buffer block: flushes after at least one data use. A word write clears it.

struct.name: BUF_INFLIGHT_REG
struct.doc: Performance counter, per even buffer block: bus clocks a request spent in flight. A word write clears it.

struct.name: BUF_MATCH_LOWER_REG
struct.doc: Read response buffer address match, lower word.

struct.name: BUF_MATCH_UPPER_REG
struct.doc: Read response buffer address match, upper word: buffer state flags and the upper address and byte enables.

struct.name: BUF_MAX_LATENCY_REG
struct.doc: Performance counter, per even buffer block: longest request latency in bus clocks. A word write clears it.

struct.name: BUF_MAX_RETRY_REG
struct.doc: Performance counter, per even buffer block: largest retry count for one request. A word write clears it.

struct.name: BUF_PREFETCH_REG
struct.doc: Performance counter, per even buffer block: requests from the prefetcher. A word write clears it.

struct.name: BUF_TOTAL_RETRY_REG
struct.doc: Performance counter, per even buffer block: PCI retries that matched the buffer tag. A word write clears it.

struct.name: BUS_TIMEOUT_REG
struct.doc: PIO retry control: retry hold-off and retry count for programmed I/O to the PCI bus. IRIX clears the low ten bits for one specific device pair (meaning unknown).

struct.name: CMD_WORD_REG
struct.doc: Held Crosstalk command word. Same layout is used for the bus-side error word and the link-side error word (request FIFO overflow, unexpected response).

struct.name: CONTROL_REG
struct.doc: Widget control. Fields from the register structure plus the mask definitions in bridge.h for the bits the structure leaves reserved (bus, device and function number, parity enables, no-snoop and relaxed ordering). IRIX attach writes bits 55:48, 31:29 and 21 (see README, "Control register").

struct.name: DEVICE_REG
struct.doc: Per-device control. Bit 19 is swap_direct (README, "Device-register bit 19").

struct.name: DIR_MAP_REG
struct.doc: Direct map: relocates a 2 GiB PCI window onto Crosstalk. IRIX writes widget at 23:20, offset at 16:0 (in units of 2 GiB) and bit 17 only for a translation equal to 0x20000000.

struct.name: ERR_INT_VIEW_REG
struct.doc: Error interrupt view: records an error whether or not it is enabled. Cleared by any write to the interrupt reset register.

struct.name: ERR_LOWER_REG
struct.doc: Widget error address, lower word: the address held when a bus-side error is logged; bits 47:32 repeat the upper word.

struct.name: ERR_UPPER_REG
struct.doc: Widget error address, upper word: the upper 16 address bits held when a bus-side error is logged. Held until the error group is cleared.

struct.name: ID_REG
struct.doc: Widget identification. Layout of the JTAG-style identification word: revision, part number, manufacturer. Bit 0 has no field in the header. The compare value in the SN2 PROM for the low twelve bits is 0x049, which would make bit 0 read one (inferred, see README).

struct.name: INT_ADDR_REG
struct.doc: Per-pin host address: 48-bit destination address and the 8-bit vector (bit position) in the host register.

struct.name: INT_DEST_LOWER_REG
struct.doc: Interrupt destination, lower word: full destination address and the target widget. IRIX reads and writes target widget bits 51:48.

struct.name: INT_DEST_UPPER_REG
struct.doc: Interrupt destination, upper word: the high 16 bits of the host address plus the target widget.

struct.name: INT_DEVICE_REG
struct.doc: Interrupt device select: three bits per pin naming the device whose buffers a pin interrupt flushes. IRIX attach writes 0x6db6db, which is device 3 in every field.

struct.name: INT_ENABLE_REG
struct.doc: Interrupt enable: bit n enables the status bit n. The header says all bits are zero after reset. IRIX attach ORs in 0x00003eff7ffffe00 (bits 30:9, 39:32 and 45:41); bit 40 (arbitration failure) and the low byte stay clear.

struct.name: INT_HOST_ERR_REG
struct.doc: Host error field: the bit position in the host interrupt register that an error sets.

struct.name: INT_MODE_REG
struct.doc: Interrupt mode: one bit per pin. IRIX attach writes zero.

struct.name: INT_RESET_REG
struct.doc: Interrupt reset: write only. A one at an error bit clears that bit and rearms the error registers; bit 6 clears the multiple-error indication. Bits 6:0 carry the Bridge-family group strobes in bridge.h and 0x7f clears all of them: IRIX attach writes 0x7f. Whether a PIC honours the group strobes is unknown (README, "Open").

struct.name: INT_STATUS_REG
struct.doc: Interrupt status: read only. Bits 7:0 are the live level of the eight interrupt pins. The remaining bits latch error conditions when the matching enable bit is set. Bits 45:42 are named in bridge.h but are reserved in the register structure.

struct.name: LINK_ERR_ADDR_REG
struct.doc: Link-side error address.

struct.name: LLP_CFG_REG
struct.doc: Link-layer configuration; valid on the first bus only (head 0).

struct.name: MAP_FAULT_REG
struct.doc: Page map fault address: PCI address bits 21:4 and device number of a translation that faulted.

struct.name: MULT_INT_REG
struct.doc: Multiple interrupt: set when a condition recurs before it is cleared. Bit 6 of the reset register clears it.

struct.name: PCIX_ERR_ATTR_REG
struct.doc: PCI-X error attribute (the 2.4-era offset list and the Altix structure differ on where it sits; IRIX reaches the bus error attribute at 0x608). Assuming the split-completion and DMA-request error attributes (0x620, 0x628) share the layout is inferred from the names only.

struct.name: PCIX_READ_BUF_ATTR_REG
struct.doc: PCI-X read buffer attribute.

struct.name: PCIX_TIMEOUT_REG
struct.doc: PCI-X read request timeout error pointer (read buffer structure and location). The 2.4-era offset list puts it in the low register page, but the Altix structure puts the PCI-X error group at 0x600 and up. Which slot holds this layout is unknown (README, revision differences).

struct.name: PCIX_WRITE_BUF_ATTR_REG
struct.doc: PCI-X write buffer attribute.

struct.name: PCIX_WRITE_BUF_VALID_REG
struct.doc: PCI-X write buffer valid cache lines.

struct.name: PCI_ERR_LOWER_REG
struct.doc: PCI bus error address, lower word, with the requester identity. IRIX reads it for the bus address of the error.

struct.name: PCI_ERR_UPPER_REG
struct.doc: PCI bus error address, upper word, with the requester identity.

struct.name: RAM_PERR_REG
struct.doc: Internal RAM parity error log: failing entry address and per-RAM error flags.

struct.name: REQ_TIMEOUT_REG
struct.doc: Request timeout reload value. The timer ticks every 32 PCI clocks (960 ns at 33 MHz). IRIX writes 0x750 on revision 1 only.

struct.name: RESP_CLEAR_REG
struct.doc: Read response buffer clear: write a one to discard a buffer.

struct.name: RESP_ERR_LOWER_REG
struct.doc: Response-buffer error address, lower word, with the device and buffer number.

struct.name: RESP_ERR_UPPER_REG
struct.doc: Response-buffer error address, upper word, with the device and buffer number of the failing entry.

struct.name: RESP_STATUS_REG
struct.doc: Read response buffer status: one valid bit and one in-use bit per buffer.

struct.name: RRB_EVEN_REG
struct.doc: Read response buffer allocation, even devices. Buffers 0,2,...,14, four bits each: enable, 2-bit virtual channel, device-pair bit.

struct.name: RRB_ODD_REG
struct.doc: Read response buffer allocation, odd devices. Buffers 1,3,...,15, four bits each.

struct.name: STATUS_REG
struct.doc: Widget status. Bus-side status. Bits 35:33 carry the PCI-X mode report; the low byte is the live level of the miscellaneous PCI inputs.

struct.name: TEST_PIN_CTRL_REG
struct.doc: Test pin control: selects output function and value for the test pins. Diagnostic only.

struct.name: TYPE1_CFG_REG
struct.doc: Type-1 configuration address bits: supplies the secondary bus and device number of a type-1 configuration cycle.
